headline: Meta chief executive Mark Zuckerberg has admitted that Meta committed to AI spending in the hundreds of billions of dollars before knowing whether it would pay off.
score_reason: Pool 8 lowered by 1: the podcast was posted Monday 12 Oct, before the 13 Oct window, and it is a recollection of past doubt, not a new decision.
importance_line: A chief executive saying plainly that a bet of this size was made without proof it would work matters first to Meta's shareholders waiting for returns, then to the suppliers and rivals building on the same assumption, but it is his recollection of past doubts, not a sign that the spending has failed.
summary: Bloomberg reports that Mark Zuckerberg, chief executive of Meta Platforms, said on the Cheeky Pint podcast, posted Monday 12 Oct, that Meta had to commit to spending hundreds of billions of dollars on the infrastructure for its AI products before it knew whether they would succeed, recalling that he put the cheque at "$100 billion or $200 billion" and asked Alexandr Wang, Meta's chief AI officer, "You sure this is going to work?". The Hindustan Times adds that Wang answered that it was "not clear at all" that it would work, that Meta's chief financial officer Susan Li warned of the cost of failure, and that Meta reports its next results after the market close on 21 Oct.
notes: Bloomberg page showed only its opening lines (paywall); the details come from the Hindustan Times (https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/us-news/zuckerberg-reveals-uncertainty-behind-meta-s-200-billion-ai-push-as-investors-await-returns-101791923062177.html), which reports the same podcast. The podcast itself was not opened.
